messages:
Maya Li: Heads-up — ACME POC blocked. Okta SSO fails with NameID errors and SCIM provisioning returns 403. Demo is on Friday, need unblock.

Samir Khan: Can you paste the exact SAML error from Okta? Also tell us whether you uploaded SP metadata from Console or we provided IdP metadata.

ACME-Okta-Admin: Okta shows `No NameID in assertion` and `NameIDFormat mismatch`. We imported your SP metadata yesterday.

Samir Khan: Common cause: NameID format set to `Unspecified`. Change it to `EmailAddress` and map `user.email` to NameID in the Okta SAML app. Use these values in Okta:
- ACS URL: https://console.redwood-inference.com/saml/acs
- Entity ID: https://console.redwood-inference.com/saml/metadata

ACME-Okta-Admin: Changed NameID to EmailAddress, SAML now completes and we can log in with SSO. However SCIM pushes still get 403.

Samir Khan: SCIM 403 typically token/role related. Ensure you're using the SCIM token (starts with `scim_`) generated in Console, not a general API key. When you create the token select the `Provisioner` role. Also confirm Okta is calling the hosted SCIM base URL: `https://api.redwood-inference.com/scim/v2` and that the Authorization header is `Authorization: Bearer scim_<token>`.

Samir Khan: Quick validation curl (replace token):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer scim_<token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood-inference.com/scim/v2/Users
```

ACME-Okta-Admin: Ran that and got 403 with body `{ "detail": "token missing org provisioning role" }`. We regenerated a token but same error.

Samir Khan: If body says missing provisioning role you're creating a token without the Provisioner role. In Console: Org Settings -> Integrations -> SCIM -> Generate token -> Role: select `Provisioner` (or `Admin`). Tokens are single-use for rotation; delete old tokens.

Samir Khan: Also check firewalls — hosted SCIM endpoints come from our IPs and Okta needs to reach them. Allowlist these (hosted): 34.72.12.5, 34.72.12.6, 34.72.12.7. If ACME is using a private VPC/air-gapped setup, the SCIM base URL will be tenant-specific and reachable only inside their network. In that case we either (a) configure a connector for outbound provisioning, or (b) expose the SCIM endpoint over the customer VPN.

ACME-Okta-Admin: We recreated the token and explicitly chose Provisioner role — curl now returns 200 and lists users. Okta pushes succeeded and new users appear in Console. SSO + SCIM green. Thanks.

Maya Li: Great. For Friday demo they want 6 users added — good to go. Also ACME asked about Dedicated POC pricing and whether SSO + SCIM works with Private/VPC.

Jules Martin: Dedicated POC checklist I'll send:
- Network: open outbound to management plane (management.redwood-inference.com) on 443 OR install connector.
- SCIM endpoint: tenant-specific, e.g. `https://scim.<tenant>.internal/scim/v2`.
- Firewall: allow inbound from our management plane CIDR when using connector.
- SAML: ACS/EntityID will be customer-specific for private console; we'll provide SP metadata after provisioning.
- Timeline: 3-5 business days to provision eval Dedicated pool + 1-2 days for SSO cert exchange if there's an audit.
- Pricing: 2-week eval Dedicated pool >= 2 GPUs; invoice as month-pro-rated. I'll DM specifics and attach pricing sheet.

Samir Khan: Temporary workaround for immediate demo: create temporary console invites or a scoped API key for devs (scope: sessions:create, users:read). Make sure to rotate/delete after demo.

support-bot: Ticket INC-2025-887 created for ACME SSO/SCIM POC; assigned to Samir Khan and Jules Martin.

ACME-Okta-Admin: Verified end-to-end with Provisioner token and NameID=email. Demo confirmed for Friday. Appreciate the rapid help :tada:

Maya Li: Closing loop. Jules, please send the Dedicated POC checklist and pricing in the sales thread. Samir — thanks for the on-call assist.
